body:
DESIGNED WITH MYK IN CHAT, 2026-08-19. OPENS AT THE DESIGN STAGE: the working spec is the
deliverable and no implementation code is written until his word.

MYK'S FRAMING, which is the whole ticket: "there must be some THING somewhere which is resolved
based on those deltas, right? ... if two deltas assign two different names to the same thing, what
does the resolver say? That's the tool we reach for."

He is right, and the measurement says the tool is not being reached for. `readRegistrations` resolves
the binding table by HAND:

    latest.set([key, lensNameOf(cand)].join(NUL_SEP), cand); // ground order: last write wins

That is a Policy — `pick byTimestamp desc` — implemented in bespoke code rather than declared as one.
Data gets the full Policy vocabulary; LAW is special-cased with one hardcoded rule.

WHAT COLLAPSES IF THE BINDING TABLE IS A RESOLVED READING. Every question this arc has been
hand-answering becomes a Policy question, and three open tickets stop being separate problems:
- two deltas naming different things the same name -> the receiver CHOOSES: `pick byTimestamp desc`
  (latest wins), `pick byAuthorRank` (mine outranks a peer's), or `conflicts` (surface both and
  refuse to guess). T198's collision and T197's sibling-lens collapse are both this.
- two deltas naming one thing differently -> `pick`, and both names resolve. That IS T198's fix.
- `byAuthorRank` is the federation answer already in the vocabulary. No adoption guard, no parking,
  no invented collision rules. THE PREFIX STOPS BEING A SAFETY MECHANISM and becomes a default label
  — "a name is just a name" (Myk).

AND THE SECOND HALF, which Myk found the same morning: THE BINDING IS IN THE WRONG PLACE. §46's
bindArrived calls `gw.adoptLaw(...)` on the RECEIVER's gateway, and adoption publishes into that
gateway's PRIMARY GROUND. So today the peer's DATA lives in its container and the peer's LAW binds at
the root — backwards from §28, where effectiveness is a property of a container. T189 scoped the
READS to the pool and left the binding store-wide, and that seam is where these defects fall through.

Myk: "the law in the dropped container only binds within the container, so if the container is
dropped shouldn't this question dissolve?" It should, and it does:
- T199 (a severed channel's lens fell back to the receiver's ground) STOPS EXISTING — drop the
  container, drop its bindings. The fail-closed guard shipped on t186 becomes belt-and-braces.
- T198's collision largely stops existing — two peers' identical law competes for one store-wide
  namespace only because bindings are store-wide. Per container, `alice:Note` and `bob:Note` are two
  containers each holding one binding, competing for nothing.
- the invariant inverts to ONE LAW PER (CONTAINER, NAME), never one name per law.

THE BOOTSTRAP IS THE REAL QUESTION, and it is why the code is hand-rolled. Resolving through a
Schema needs a Schema, and Schemas come from registrations — `replayRegistrations` builds the registry
the machinery reads from. Law-about-law has to start somewhere the fixpoint can reach.

MEASURED PRECEDENT: §8 already does this. Trust is data, and trust.ts resolves its roster through the
SUBSTRATE — an `inView` predicate "over the very declaration deltas admission reads — one live lens".
So a constitutional table CAN be a resolved reading rather than bespoke code, and genesis is where its
base law lives.

MEASURED GAP, stated so nobody plans around a precedent that does not stretch: `inView` is a
PREDICATE, and trust.ts says so in its own words — "the inView lens cannot validate any of this (a
predicate sees pointers, not shape rules)". A Policy-resolved View is a step BEYOND inView. Whether
that step is an afternoon or an arc is the first thing the working spec must answer, and it decides
the scope of everything above.

TICKETS THIS WOULD FOLD: T197, T198 (second half), T199, and the binding half of T193.

TIER: design-stage, so Myk's merge. He asked for a working spec with user stories rather than a chat
design, and the criteria must name their verification as always.
title: Law resolves like data — the binding table as a resolved reading, scoped to its container
